newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr eases vs mark, yen in Tokyo after brief rally.
newsitem.headline: Dlr eases vs mark, yen in Tokyo after brief rally.

text.p: The dollar eased against the mark and the yen in late Tokyo trading on Friday after a brief rally led by mark selling by a major public operator, traders said.

The dollar briefly rose to 1.7041 mark on large-lot purchases by a major public investor and other buying based on rekindled speculation that European countries will eventually have to ease fiscal criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU), traders said.
Some said that the large dollar buying for the mark may have come from Russia, which is becoming active in the market.
The dollar/mark upswing briefly pushed the dollar up to a day high of 116.78 yen.
But soon afterwards it eased to around 1.7000 mark as profit taking set in, traders said.

At the same time, the dollar fell to 116.30 yen, partly due to a wire service report quoting a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official as saying that even if the dollar fell below 110 yen, it would not cause a rash of losses by Japanese companies.
At 0825 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.7000/05 marks and 116.32/42 yen.
